items.body:
1970 (April 10th, 1970 – IBC Studios, London)

Negotiations were now underway between Sean Murphy and several labels including Deram, CBS and Harvest, the EMI sub-label that had distributed Volume Two in the UK and already had Kevin Ayers in its stable. “They are still not an attraction in the very top bracket, so it was a pleasant surprise to see major companies throwing in genuinely massive bids earlier this year when the group was looking for a recording deal,” Richard Williams revealed. Ultimately, Soft Machine signed with CBS, but Third was self-financed, taken partly from studio sessions, but also from live recordings (“Facelift”) and edits and loops of tapes made by Mike Ratledge and Hugh Hopper at the home of Bob Woolford, who had let them use his Brenell and Stellavox tape recorders. Such infringements of accepted professional practices were only possible because CBS, having acquired a finished album, were no longer in a position to force the band to comply with them.

The benefit for Soft Machine in terms of artistic freedom is easy to measure. But this has to be balanced against the fact that the production on Third is, to put it bluntly, an unmitigated disaster. IBC, at the time the studio of choice for such notorious perfectionists as The Who and the Bee Gees, are probably less to blame than the band themselves who, in spite of the issues with Volume Two, are again credited as sole producers. The sound suffers from almost constantly saturated low frequencies and extremely vague mediums, the drums are much too low in the mix, as if played behind a closed door; and the organ is deprived of much of its biting impact through overwhelming equalization. Unfortunately the 2007 remaster, while an improvement, fails to rectify this.

What is problematic is that, as well as making the album an uncomfortable listen, its sub-par production lessens the claim, widely held at the time of its release, that Third represented musical state-of-the-art. This claim was based on Soft Machine’s ability, unparalleled among their contemporaries, to draw from and amalgamate an exceptionally wide range of influences. Starting out as a rock band, and then gradually moving towards jazz to invent a uniquely personal, and absolutely valid, British answer to American fusion, Soft Machine went even further, incorporating the influence of Stockhausen’s avant-garde and Terry Riley’s repetitive minimalism. Third’s ‘total’ vision, encompassing the entire spectrum of known musical genres, placed Soft Machine at the forefront of musical “progress” in 1970. However, horizons have since expanded to such an extent, beyond the Western tradition in particular, that this concept of universality has aged considerably.

In his insightful review of Third for Actuel, Paul Alessandrini wrote of “music to really listen to, no longer aiming for a purely physical vibration, more interiorized. Soft Machine have re-thought their musical influences – Riley, Cecil Taylor, Coltrane – to really make them their own, abandoning their aesthetics of random explosion in favor of a much more thought-out approach.” There are still occasional reminders of these sonic excesses that, as Alessandrini noted, had now largely disappeared from their music. Mike Ratledge's lengthy solo introduction to “Facelift” almost sounds like an electric exorcism, as if to rid Soft Machine of what still remains of that violence in order to reinvent their music in a more controlled manner, setting formal perfection as their new objective.

Considered as a whole, Hugh Hopper's piece represents the last remnant of Soft Machine’s early days, when they still favored spirit over form - here found lacking in both sound quality and performance, with a few train wrecks along the way - and were intent on disregarding the accepted rules. “Facelift” includes free sections increasingly at odds with Ratledge’s preoccupation with structure – and while as a keyboard player, he still embodies the band’s more radical leanings, Ratledge’s own compositions reveal a much less iconoclastic temperament. Hopper described his own approach at the time as “halfway between” that of Dean, “whose thing is really total improvisation, without any structure, and on the other extreme, [that of Ratledge] who's into entirely formalized musical forms.

“Moon in June” completes Robert Wyatt’s donation to Soft Machine of the material originally intended for his first solo album in 1968. It is interesting to note that Wyatt does this at the exact point where Soft Machine had shed any remaining reference to pop in their live repertoire. Looking back, Wyatt was certainly justified in saying that his side of Third was “the last chance I had to use all the things we'd done without being a jazz band. I wanted to get twenty minutes of it down somewhere.” And since his colleagues, reluctant to act as mere accompanists, had made no secret of their lack of interest in his songs, he recorded most of “Moon in June” on his own, repeating the modus operandi of the 1968-69 demo. Hugh Hopper and Mike Ratledge’s participation is again limited to the organ solo halfway through (Hopper also plays a short melodic theme earlier in the piece). Elton Dean wasn’t asked to contribute anything – Wyatt’s unconvincing justification being that he “hadn’t yet worked out how to work on [his] stuff with the added wind instruments.”

As there was no mention of this breach of band discipline in the sleeve notes, only the most astute listeners noticed that the organ heard during the first ten minutes was a Hammond rather than Ratledge’s signature Lowrey, that the playing clearly wasn’t Ratledge’s, and that most of the ‘bass’ parts were played on an electric piano. When the truth was finally revealed, Wyatt gave contradictory versions of what had happened – in one interview claiming that Ratledge and Hopper had “refused to play [on “Moon in June”] and I had to play it all myself,” in another that he’d “almost had to force them to get them to play on it, which I thought was rather unfair as I’d done my best to get into the music they were writing.” Probably the most objective and believable of Wyatt’s rationales was that he was “terrified it’d be played wrong” if he didn’t perform it all himself.

To approach “Moon in June” as a ‘message’ song would misrepresent Wyatt’s more mundane intent, insofar as the phonetic qualities of the words often seem to matter more to him than their meaning. In other words, “Moon in June” is above all a musical composition, a suite of instrumental sections, some of which are adorned with melodies and lyrics, and others not. The singing accompanies the music rather than vice-versa. In this respect, outside of a possible rivalry with Elton Dean and Wyatt’s inability to sing while drumming, there was no theoretical incompatibility between Soft Machine’s move towards jazz and the continued presence of Wyatt’s voice (even if limited to the Echoplexed scat singing of his solitary interludes during the band’s concerts). Dispensing with vocals was the single most questionable move in Soft Machine’s entire musical evolution, not to mention one whose commercial consequences cannot be underestimated. In different circumstances, Hugh Hopper would surely have joined Wyatt in lobbying for having at least some vocals, but in addition to his increasingly strained personal relationship with Wyatt, Hopper had at this point completely lost interest in non-instrumental music. “I find that using the human voice means asserting limitations to your music right from the start”, he explained in 1972. “I am more interested in the sounds generated by instruments, or electronic devices, because the possibilities offered by songs are much more limited than when experimenting with sounds.”

Even if there was no future for singing in Soft Machine, “Moon in June” at least offers evidence that Robert Wyatt, in a voice-free context, could still be more than “a session drummer for an interesting new species of jazz groups,” as long as he contributed to the writing. When it came to extended pieces, he could stand comparison with Mike Ratledge, even though he lacked any comparable academic background. In addition to its constant melodic inspiration, “Moon in June” is very skillfully constructed (indeed, its instrumental architecture had remained intact since 1968), and confirms Wyatt’s seemingly innate talent for making a coherent whole out of ill-assorted musical ideas.

items._cn_summary: 这张1970年的专辑是英国Canterbury乐派代表乐队Soft Machine的里程碑之作。乐评详述了乐队与CBS签约的幕后过程，以及他们如何利用厂牌的发行模式获得了前所未有的艺术自由度，自主制作了这张概念专辑。音乐上融合了爵士融合、Stockhausen的先锋派与Terry Riley的简约重复元素，被当时视为音乐前沿的'全景式'视野，跨越从摇滚到爵士再至现代音乐多种类型。录音制作存在明显缺陷：低频饱和、中频模糊、鼓声被压低、管风琴的冲击力被削弱，2007年再版未能完全修复。乐评也指出，随着全球音乐视野在西方传统之外的拓展，这种'普世性'的概念已有所褪色。尽管制作短板明显，其跨越流派的实验性融合在当时具有开创意义，对理解Canterbury乐派的演进有重要参考价值。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items._cn_summary: 这张合辑汇集了圣多美和普林西比两个非洲小岛在七、八十年代录制却较少为人所知的Puxa风格作品。该风格将merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等多种节奏元素融于一炉，多把吉他交织缠绕，主唱与和声彼此呼应，构成一套既能充盈舞池又能召唤或驱逐精神力量的复合音乐体系。乐评特别提到Pedro Lima领衔的乐队以闷音吉他律动与鼓手对位，键盘和贝斯退场后仅留鼓与吉他驱动舞者的场面，以及Africa Negra等人的作品如何在长时间现场演奏中铺展流动的律动。文末也简述了殖民背景、葡萄牙殖民统治与加勒比隔海地理对岛上音乐风格的塑形作用，指出两个小小岛屿在录音资源匮乏下依然孕育出规模与质量不成比例的独特音乐场景。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: Analog Africa厂牌推出的这张合辑聚焦贝宁传奇人物Antoine Dougbé及其与Orchestre Poly-Rythmo的合作，时间跨度为1977至1982年。Dougbé以拍腿打出Cavacha节奏著称，该节奏由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车节拍中提炼，后蔓延至1970年代中期的刚果流行乐。Dougbé本人被称为"魔鬼首相"，也是伏都教信徒，对乐手要求严苛，最终只与Poly-Rythmo长期合作。合辑收录其三张专辑及部分单曲，展现出融合贝宁传统伏都音乐、古巴son风格与刚果伦巴的多重影响。编曲方面，合成器铺底与塑料质感的吉他音色相互交织，标志性的高帽节奏贯穿始终，cowbell与鼻音式人声呼应构成浓郁的跨大西洋对话。与厂牌此前发行的Poly-Rythmo合辑相比，此作更突出古巴son的渗透痕迹，是非洲流行音乐跨国流动的重要文献。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 乐队以废物利用的方式手工制作乐器，从碎料杂物中构建了包括厨房号、tassofon、clarinut 等奇异乐器，并以惊人的准确音准呈现于录音中。专辑延续首作的多元风格混搭，将克莱兹默、昆比亚、桑巴、非洲节拍与中东旋律融入同一框架。不同曲目采用对应文化风格的主奏乐器配以即兴段落，展现了演奏者扎实的器乐技巧。整体上，这张作品以打破乐器物质边界的实验精神出发，探讨了音乐作为人类共通语言的主题，同时提醒人们音乐的本质不在于器材的奢华，而在于创造与表达的欲望。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是挪威Camilla Hole Trio在延续前作科幻合成器探索后，转向更为扎根传统的新作。主奏乐器高音萨克斯结合爵士语汇，将挪威西部民间舞曲曲调作为即兴起点。乐评聚焦于开场曲的解构方式：旋律最初由萨克斯奏出，叠加贝斯手Kalman的模块合成器与鼓手Nesheim的颤音琴作为色彩层；随后角色边界消解，贝斯手接过旋律线与萨克斯齐奏，鼓手扩展节奏维度，整体在民谣曲调骨架上展开自由的即兴发挥。三重奏的核心特质在于成员间角色的持续流动与重组，不拘泥于传统主奏—伴奏格局，使一首民间舞曲演变为开放式的当代爵士即兴文本。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由丹麦三人组合GuldGanger推出的数字EP，由北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目以传统音乐为底色，融入锯琴、风笛、扬琴、长笛与弦乐等多样乐器，呈现出古老而生涩的氛围。开场曲《Svennedal》以粗犷的节奏展示主唱极具说服力的声线；唯一原创作品《Nordgård》由成员Morten Musicus创作，锯琴与风笛推动出强烈的行进感。扬琴在传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》中提供细腻底色，终曲《Ormsø》则以器乐形式融合锯琴、长笛与弦乐，营造出活泼而不失怪异的声响。整体展现出乐队超越新人水准的成熟度，为后续全长专辑留下期待空间。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single �A hist�ria de nossa l�ngua� features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including �Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapu�, Ipanema, Maracan�, Capoeira, etc.� This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer�s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track �Ver meu povo se abra�ar� to the convincing reggae of the second single, �Que seja um reggae�. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, �Independ�ncia� features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings �Battre des ailes� accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on �Dans le sud feat�. The gentle �Strati di tempo� is the closest to Santtana�s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz In�cio Lula da Silva�s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political.� For example, on �L�nguas Gerais,� French rapper Oxmo Puccino �speaks about colonization.� Continuing to quote from the liner notes, �Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.� Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing �Cocanha� in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out.� � Like his popular previous recording O Para�so (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Para�so , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message. Find the artist online.

items._cn_summary: Lucas Santtana 历经九年专辑积累与二十五年世界音乐生涯，以《Brasiliano》展开对巴西语言与文化多样性的音乐探索。专辑以葡语、法语、英语、西班牙语、奥克语、佛得角克里奥尔语及图皮-瓜拉尼语等多种语言演唱，邀请各国词作者与歌手参与，呈现巴西作为文化交汇点的历史脉络。开篇曲与巴西国宝级音乐人 Gilberto Gil 合作，以语言拟人化的方式追溯葡萄牙语从拉丁语系的演化轨迹，并在歌词中融入伊帕内玛、马拉卡纳等承载原住民记忆的地名。整体制作以手工质感乐器为主，木管、鼓皮、弦线与人声交织，配以合成器与 mellotron 增添现代光泽，风格从活泼的派对曲到雷鬼均有触及。这张专辑既是国际协作的庆典，也因 Gil 的政治经历而带有鲜明的社会议题表达，是一张兼具文化深度与可听性的跨界世界音乐作品。

items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑记录了马里两位音乐家2013年的原始二重奏录音，后由制作人Nick Gold（曾促成Ali Farka Touré与Toumani Diabaté的合作）主导重新编曲，加入弦乐、mellotron、吉他、打击乐及人声叠加。巴拉风与n'goni这两种马里乐器的罕见组合构成了核心，在重新制作中保留了原始即兴骨架，同时通过器乐层次扩展形成开放式的合奏编排。开篇曲目以人声开篇，n'goni提供循环riff，巴拉风即兴漂浮其上，弦乐仅作点缀式节奏动机而不喧宾夺主。Yeredon Bali则展现了曼丁哥音乐典型的对唱结构。整体处理虽激进但在音乐性上保持了分寸感，是对马里传统器乐组合边界的一次有意义探索。

items.body:
Photo: Claudia de Ventura
Crete�s Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island�s best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. Its three bowed strings are stopped by the fingernails of the non-bowing hand rather than being pressed to the fingerboard. Its sound hovers on the enticing edge between fundamental and harmonics.
Petrakis is also a leading luthier, making the lyras and the other instruments he plays, including the traditional metal-strung lute laouto, and in conjunction with Ross Daly he�s developed and plays a range of lyras with ringing sympathetic strings.
True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature to Petrakis, in music of rich lyricism, in melody and texture.
�Astro Sti Gaza� (�Star in Gaza�), a wish for peace written by Petrakis with lyrics by his brother Yannis Petrakis, opens the album. At first a string drone, then Petrakis�s laouto and lyra, Ma�lle Duchemin�s harp, Pavlos Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the percussion of Iranian Bijan Chemirani, who plays frame and flask hand-drums on most tracks. The dark, sinuous instrumental line is tracked by the husky vocal of Giorgis Xylouris, who sings on three tracks, the other six being instrumental. �Nathenas,� a traditional Cretan song in asymmetric rhythms, has a powerful ensemble of lyra, laouto, frame-drum, stick-hit davul, topped out by Breton Sylvain Barou�s reeds and Armenian shvi whistle.
�Anglianico,� a stately melody composed by Petrakis, has the tremolo mandolins of Valencian musician Efr�n L�pez and Michalis Kontaxakis in an elegant almost orchestral sound with lyra, guitars (Antonis Voumvoulakis and Samuel Mele), Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the accordion of Mattia Marco Gregoriadis on whose improvisation the tarantella-like �Pukan� is based.
Chemirani is particularly featured on his composition �Panj Pol,� a short finger-rippling, slapping solo on zarb flask-drum whose rhythm is the foundation for the song that it breaks into, �Agrilos,� by Petrakis with lyrics by brother Yannis celebrating the wine-producing district of Crete where they grew up. It develops into a big sound of massed instruments, with a break on frame-drum and Sakir Oran Uygan�s big double-headed davul drum before a surge of squealing tulum bagpipe and other wind instruments from Barou.
�Evlerin �n� Mersin,� a traditional tune from Asia Minor, has a march-like feel, beginning with keening lyra over a slow, inexorable drum pulse, building to soaring epic as more instruments join, peaking with Barou�s zurnas. �Muixeranga,� again with a steady, imposing pulse, is an anthemic tune played in Valencia during the Muixeranga, the traditional building of excitingly high pyramidal human towers in which the big and strong form the bottom layers and the youngest and lightest clamber up to form the topmost. Petrakis intends the track as a message of support to Valencia following the climate-change-driven floods of 2024.
Preluded and accompanied by ringing 3/4 time arpeggiating plucked strings and percussion, with the melody played on lyra, the source of �Nothing Else Matters,� is unexpected: it�s a beautiful version, evocative of memory and perhaps sadness, of a Metallica number.

Thrace: Sunday Morning Sessions
Ettore Castagna:

items._cn_summary: 克里特岛里拉琴演奏家兼制琴师 Stelios Petrakis 的专辑《Lyric》以传统克里特弦乐为核心，邀请来自伊朗、布列塔尼、亚美尼亚、瓦伦西亚等地的音乐家参与跨文化合作。专辑聚焦克里特里拉琴与鲁特琴的音色特质，三弦立式持琴、指甲触弦不按指板的独特演奏方式产生基音与泛音交织的悬浮感。曲目包含为加沙祈愿和平的《Astro Sti Gaza》、以小亚细亚传统旋律为素材的《Evlerin Önü Mersin》以及描绘瓦伦西亚叠人塔庆典的《Muixeranga》。制作中融入了波斯桑图尔琴风铃鼓、亚美尼亚哨笛、布列塔尼风笛、瓦伦西亚颤音曼陀林等多种地方乐器，在保持克里特传统骨架的同时拓展了地中海周边的音乐对话空间。

items.body: Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka I n the High Middle Ages, Hildegard of Bingen said that �The truly holy person welcomes all that is earthly.� William Blake declared in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (1790) that �Exuberance is beauty.� In 1855, Walt Whitman published the poem �Song Of Myself, 51� in Leaves of Grass , which contains the famous line �I am large, I contain multitudes.� I�m just skimming the surface of mystical experience, of those struck by wonder and an all-encompassing insight into how people fit into the �grand scheme of things.� At some point on this trajectory, the boundary between the religious and the secular breaks down and simply being human becomes the ultimate wow. Which brings us to Polish artist Maria Ka�s latest album Di Mashin . Ka found that her family had Jewish roots, a discovery that led her to an immersion in Jewish studies and the Yiddish language. As on 2023�s Der Hemshekh , she unreels original songs written in Yiddish, embracing a politically active feminism and a committed meta-universality. Her musical vision is fragrantly mystical, and she presents us with a whole Yiddish cosmos. While not sharing the same type of musical style, Ka reminds me of John Zorn�s aesthetic of mixing the grotesque and the sacred into Jewish experimental music. She also reminds me of the woman on the phone sampled on Wally Brill�s Jewish cantorial electronica album The Covenant (2007), who confesses she can�t sleep after hearing someone in a bar talking about the Book of Ezekiel and being haunted by the vision of Jews arriving from a future space-time. She sees that we are all suspended in webs of relationships. She is also deeply aware of how we are subject to larger social forces and structures � which sometimes must be met with radical action -- that are the machinery of life. There is a heavy dose of electro and punkish attitude spinning through her musical universe. Ostensibly, the album is divided between electronic and rock tracks, but there is a consistency to the sound that is united in loopy joy. At its best, Di Mashin is sly and sexy. Opening track �Alef � Tsentauri Disko� finds Ka in the city, musing on the seaside, wriggling like a snake at night, and watching Gdańsk wake up. �I often Dream about Cosmos, about the Land above the Earth / overhead / Alef Centauri Jewish disco!� she sings, set to a thumping urban electro grind. (See video below) Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �Vos iz dos?� is a standout, more in the �rock� vein, with Ka howling a debate over the Yiddish language itself. Perhaps it is based in a critique that she received, as she starts with What is this? Maria, what is this? I constantly hear it, it has not finished You speak no Yiddish!/ It�s so easy! Your language is incorrect, mistaken is your speech and dialect! � Given that Ka is producing new modern songs in Yiddish, there is something disarming in acknowledging the tension over who might claim ownership of language itself. Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �SuperNove� might remind listeners of Jacob wrestling with God, if that battle was done to an �80s new wave beat. Ka has visions of the past, the Old World and old demons, and she fights a ghost that rises to block her way: � I fought him with Strength, punched him with my both hands�I triumphed over him! I myself � I did triumph over him! � And after that victory, � it�s a great Surprise � the Past melted in the Cosmic Blast! � Ka also seems to be challenging herself, pointing in new directions. �Di Kosmish motorn (Cosmic engines)� brought to mind the former Warsaw Village Band�s blues-influenced singer Maja Kleszcz. Depeche Mode�s (fronted by Dave Gahan, of Jewish ancestry) forays into fusing electronica with blues might be another touchpoint. Hearing the cosmic engines like a modern day Pythagoras, she is awestruck by hearing the cosmic engines in her head. �Dos geverk (The mechanism)� offers some grinding guitars to convey the constant motion of the daily rat race � echoed later on by the title track, �Di Mashin (The Machine),� which peels back the layers of society to reveal the incessant obsession for money. The music of �The Machine� is hyperspeed cabaret, close to madness. The system demands more money � but she indicates that she is a spanner in the works, working to bring it down: � I watch the machine�s death / Full and steadily red is my hand in the end. � Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka Feminist politics come to the fore on �Ikh bin a froy (I am a woman),� and Ka reminds me a bit of the divine Ms. H of Bingen chanting over a motoric beat. She refuses to be hemmed in by structures, signaling that the Forest is her home, the stars her friends; �I wake up every day / and new scroll create.� Album closer �Di milkhome� (War)� is more future blues, transposing war, empty shipyards, and advice from her mother that all miseries will end and freedom will navigate the turmoil �like huge ships at Sea.� Di Mashin is possessed by such a singular offbeat vision and personal mythology that I wonder where Maria Ka will take her Yiddishfuturism next�Perhaps beyond our solar system, grooving on an interstellar plane with her band wriggling like snakes. Find the artist online. Further listening: Maria Ka - Der Hemshekh Warsaw Village Band & Bassałyki - Sploty WoWaKin - Kraj za miastem

items._cn_summary: 波兰艺术家Maria Ka在《Di Mashin》中以意第绪语演唱原创歌曲，融合电子律动与朋克态度，回应她发现家族犹太血统后投身意第绪文化的历程。专辑在电子曲目与摇滚曲目之间切换，却被一种循环往复的喜悦统一。开场曲《Alef – Tsentauri Disko》以都市电子研磨节拍包裹天文意象；《Vos iz dos?》则转向摇滚质地，以咆哮式演唱对意第绪语本身展开辩论，回应外界对其语言正統性的质疑。整体呈现出神圣与怪诞交织的气质，与John Zorn的犹太实验美学形成回响，同时带有女性主义政治立场，将语言存续与宇宙意识并置于同一声景之中。

items.body: The Visit by cris derksen The Visit isn�t an album built on compromises. The fourth release from Derksen, a Canadian from the North TallCree Reserve on her father�s side, and with a Mennonite lineage from her mother, pushes and cajoles her visions, where it�s the opening, full-throated improvisation of �White Gladis 1� (with singer Jennifer Kreisberg) or the encompassing haunting mood that grows up around �Lyre Birds.� She�s primarily a cellist, one who works across genres; one of the great joys here is it�s impossible to attach any kind of handle to the music. Just as you think you have it nailed down, the next track is something different, as with the the cello and programming of �aabaakwad� which becomes the wordless singing of �New Heya.� The Visit by cris derksen There�s a raw, unfettered beauty to the album, music made with passion and no restraints. There are a couple of songs here, but nothing that conforms to expectations, altering gears and direction, as when the strings and brass that arrive from nowhere to take over �Buffalo Girls.� The Visit by cris derksen But the emotional centrepiece here is �Lyre Birds,� with Derksen�s cello weaving sparely around the shards of spoken words, leading into the fluttering piano arpeggios of �Nice And Clean.� This is an album of surprises, leading down strange lanes and around brilliant corners that offer startling new views. As both composer and musician, Cris Derksen is more than a singular talent; she�s a person with a vision for her music, and she keeps true to it here. The Visit is not an easy listen, but it is eminently satisfying. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 这是加拿大大提琴家Cris Derksen的第四张专辑，融合了她的原住民（TallCree）与门诺派背景。整张专辑拒绝折衷，曲目之间频繁变换手法：从与歌手Jennifer Kreisberg合作的即兴开篇，到大提琴与编程节拍的交织，再到无歌词人声与弦乐铜管的突袭，情绪核心落在《Lyre Birds》，大提琴稀疏地围绕碎片化的语言展开，随后衔接钢琴琶音。作品强调原始、不加约束的美感，不遵循任何流派惯例，每一次转向都出乎意料。Derksen既是作曲家也是演奏者，专辑呈现清晰连贯的个人美学，虽不轻松聆听，但提供高度的满足感。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — The self titled album from My New Band Believe is a great debut from the project spearheaded by former Black Midi member Cameron Picton. An interesting foray into the worlds of prog rock mixed with chamber pop, art rock and experimental music, it is overly pastoral at times, as if the material itself was recorded in Canterbury in the early 70s. Musically fantastic, the overall guitar work really stands out, with lovely acoustic work that is akin to Steve Howe's playing in Yes's glory years. Cameron's vocals also show range and emotion than he did with Black Midi, but at times it does come off as very Dan Bejaresque. A great debut which hopefully is a path to future material. I'd give this a high 7 to low 8 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is Love Story.

items._cn_summary: 这张同名专辑是前Black Midi成员Cameron Picton的个人项目首作，将前卫摇滚与室内流行、艺术摇滚以及实验音乐融合在一起。整体氛围带有七十年代初坎特伯雷场景的田园牧歌气质，吉他表现尤为突出，木吉他演奏让人联想到Yes乐队鼎盛时期Steve Howe的手法。Cameron的嗓音展现出比在Black Midi时期更宽的音域和情感层次，某些段落则带有Dan Bejar式的处理。作为出道专辑，它在传统前卫摇滚的框架内加入了室内编配和实验性元素，但并未彻底突破类型边界，推荐曲目为Love Story。

items.body: Miami-based electronic band Astari Nite return with an exclusive remix of “Why Are You So Lame,” the lead track from last May’s Medications in Bloom EP. The remix is lovingly constructed by renowned New York City DJ, producer, musician, and engineer Hi-Fi Hillary, aka Hillary Johnson, head of Kale Shelter Studios, who also mixed and mastered the original EP. While the original version of the track is already a catchy, chorus-driven affair, the remix is a true celebration of Miami dance culture, toning down some of the original’s guitar-driven approach to allow for a glorious blend of freestyle, disco, electroclash, and EBM, all sounds which thrive in Astari Nite’s hometown. There’s even a little nod to chiptune tossed in for good measure, a welcome treat for fans of the genre. Ripe for the dance floor or for a stern strut on hot summer streets, the remix is a welcome addition to the band’s ever-growing catalogue. Johnson’s many credits over the years include recording/engineering work for bands such as Bootblacks, Liste Noire, Second Still, Angels of Light, Autodrone, My Favorite, and Bell Hollow, the latter which she also played live keyboards with. She has also recently remixed tracks by Black Rose Burning, Frenchy and the Punk, IKON, and The Long Losts and has upcoming remixes scheduled with Darkswoon, Negative Agent, and The Harrow. Astari Nite vocalist Mychael Ghost offers a few words about working with Johnson: Hillary is a genius! In fact, New York City should have a parade named after her. The love that she poured into the “Medications In Bloom” EP will never leave my heart. I explained to her how stupid I am though I would like my songs to sound like this and she did just that. Melodies I never knew existed were brought to light. Her creativity levels are fascinating. Her pure honesty is what shaped the EP and colored it wonderfully. Check out the remix below, and be sure to check in with Astari Nite on their upcoming tour. items._cn_summary: Astari Nite 这张混音作品由纽约制作人 Hi-Fi Hillary 操刀，将原曲吉他驱动的后朋克骨架重新解构，融入迈阿密夜店文化特有的自由式、迪斯科、电子冲击与EBM元素，并以chiptune点缀。原曲副歌已具朗朗上口的特质，混音版则削弱吉他比重，让合成器节奏成为主导，使作品更契合舞池与夏日街头的氛围。乐队主唱盛赞制作人的创意与真诚，称其挖掘了旋律中隐藏的光彩。整体制作精良，融合多种舞曲亚类型，属于独立暗潮场景中较为成熟的跨界尝试，但创新性较为有限，未见突破性的实验手法或独特文化视角。

items.body: Kevin Coleman has already proven himself to be one of the more adventurous artists within the cosmic Americana sphere, but with K.C.Blues, Nashville-based multi-instrumentalist progresses Appalachian and fingerstyle guitar traditions into a whole new beast. Inspired by roughened field recordings of blues and folk music from the early 20th century, this album finds Coleman further embracing spontaneity, the art of imperfection and the freedom of live improvisation and open collaboration to his expressionistic style of string music. Recorded in various non-traditional spaces with equipment that sometimes malfunctioned with friends like Trevor Nikrant (Styrofoam Winos, MJ Lenderman, Ryan Davis’s Roadhouse Band), Tommy Stangroom and J.W. Bird leaning into freeform sonic experimentation, K.C. Blues reflects a more discordant and chaotic side to Coleman’s otherwise pastoral sound. With banjo, guitar, mandolin, fiddle, lapsteel and drums commingling with a whole cornucopia of unexpected instruments from wine glasses to Gopichand and balalaika, the music here is reminiscent of everything from forgotten prewar 78s to the rustic gothic chill of Jill Tracy and the Malcontent Orchestra and the southern gothic atmosphere of 2000s-era Tom Waits. Check out the album’s first single, the dissonantly unnerving yet harrowingly beautiful soundscape that is “Ars Longa,” for a fine example of this unique experimental, mood-based folk style, with hints of European fiddle music naturally cropping up in the mix for good measure: Co-released between Centripetal Force (USA) and Ramble Records (AUS) and to be released on July 17 on vinyl, CD and digital, this is a must have for anyone who’s a fan of Pelt, Magic Tuber Stringband and the likes of Amon Düül II. Preorder your copy here (unless you’re in Australia, in which case, click here). -KH
items._genre: experimental folk / avant-garde Americana / free improvisation
items._cn_summary: 纳什维尔多乐器演奏家Kevin Coleman在这张专辑中，将阿巴拉契亚指弹吉他传统推向新的方向。灵感来自二十世纪初蓝调与民谣的田野录音，他强调即兴、留白与不完美，在非传统空间使用可能故障的设备进行自由合作录音。专辑呈现出比以往更为不和谐与混沌的声响特质，班卓琴、吉他、曼陀林、小提琴、踏板钢与鼓与各种非常规乐器——红酒杯、戈皮琴、巴拉莱卡——交织共处。整体音乐令人联想到战前被遗忘的78转唱片、Jill Tracy的乡村哥特寒意以及Tom Waits南方哥特式氛围。首支单曲展现了不和谐却极具美感的音景，并自然融入欧洲提琴音乐元素，是一张为Pelt、Magic Tuber Stringband及Amon Düül II爱好者准备的实验性作品。

items._cn_summary: 这张1987年发行的专辑以拼贴为核心手法，从十余位来自欧美日各国的实验音乐家处获取原始磁带素材，包括Merzbow、Organum、Nurse With Wound、Asmus Tietchens、Controlled Bleeding等地下场景重要人物。创作周期跨越两年，制作者对这些声音材料进行录音、组装、混音与母带处理，构建出兼具工业噪音与具体音乐特征的听觉景观。限量三百张发行，手绘封面与内页插画强调其作为实物艺术品的属性。欧洲地下厂牌Selektion出品，后由Staubgold等小厂再版。这张作品的价值在于将多位噪音与实验创作者的素材汇聚为统一的拼贴结构，是八十年代地下磁带文化交汇的典型案例。对偏好实验与暗潮交叉领域的听众具有参考意义。

items._cn_summary: 这是一张由Secret Pyramid操刀的混音作品，属于A Strangely Isolated Place厂牌Isolatedmix系列的第74期。整张混音以环境音乐与无人机音色为底色，穿插现代古典弦乐四重奏片段，包括Scelsi与Ligeti的室内乐作品，以及Penderecki的《Polymorphia》等先锋作曲。混音还收录了Abul Mogard的深沉氛围作品、Broadcast与The Focus Group的合作曲目，以及Slowdive的《Cello》等慢核元素。Alireza Mashayekhi的伊朗传统作曲片段为混音带来跨文化听觉体验。全长约65分钟，可免费下载。从内容来看，这是一份精心编排的氛围混音，兼顾古典严肃性与电子实验性，但并非原创评论文章，仅为曲目信息的罗列，缺乏作者主观分析与音乐评论深度。

items._cn_summary: 这张混音作品由Benoît Pioulard为A Strangely Isolated Place厂牌的Isolatedmix系列第六十二期操刀，跨越实验电子、原声民谣、暗黑氛围与中世纪音乐等多个领域。选曲涵盖Andrew Chalk的氛围质感、Colin Stetson的萨克斯独白、Future 3的俱乐部声响以及Saint Hildegard的格里高利圣咏片段，形成古典与当代电子的对话。整体编排强调氛围层的递进与情绪渐变，将中世纪宗教音乐与后摇氛围并置，营造出时间感模糊的聆听体验。作为免费下载的DJ混音，曲目之间的衔接体现了策划者对声音纹理与氛围流动的敏感度，是小众独立厂牌策划下的一张兼具艺术性与可听性的混音作品。

items.body: Review by Finnforest — An Italian Tea Club? Not really, of course, but from the first minute of this album, I was astounded by how much itreminded me of earlier releases from The Tea Club, one of my favorite bands in the states. More onthat later. Phil Selvini and the Mind Warp are a newer Bologna-based band formed and emergent in thepandemic years of the early 2020s. Selvini is the composer of the material and a multi-instrumentalist backed by four other excellent musicians. T.E.T.R.U.S. is their debut album title and an acronym based on words that lead to thethematic element of humanity confronting inner demons, a monster that we see depicted so well on thealbum cover art. This is a rousing modern prog sound that both pays homage to certain textures ofclassic prog but with an attitude that is heavy and modern and athletic in feel. In fact, withEnglish language vocals and few common Italian prog sound choices, there isn't much here that alignswith RPI beyond geography. This is an album suited well for fans of heavy prog, crossover, or evengeneral art rock period. As mentioned, my most obvious point of reference here would be The Tea Club from Jersey, those epicmoonlit night-walk soundtracks from the McGowan brothers. Selvini not only sounds hauntingly likethe McGowans vocally, but even the spidery guitars and the structural song elements are often prettysimilar. I'm assuming this is completely by chance and that Selvini has never heard of the Teas and,if that's true, it's even more fascinating. If you doubt me, just audio-sample the first 90 secondsof "Riding in the Fog" and tell me it doesn't sound like an outtake from Rabbit. The first four tracks are in the five to nine minute range and in my mind make up the "side A" ifyou will. "Side B" would be the monstrous 26-minute track entitled "The Mind Warp." The album isconsistent with two main sound vibes. There is the mellow side featuring acoustic or clean electricguitars and atmospheric keys that yield beautiful but haunting, lonely spaces. This penchant forthese moody spaces is my favorite part of the album. The other side of the coin is the heavy partswhich have a certain post-In Absentia Porcupine Tree vibe but a bit grittier and with moreheavy than actual metal. The heavier sections feel frantic and angular and even a little math-y attimes. These two contrasting light and heavy sides work throughout. The dark moods and even someWall-era Floyd guitar riffs contribute to a very satisfying debut indeed.
items._genre: heavy prog / art rock / modern progressive
items._cn_summary: 意大利博洛尼亚乐队Phil Selvini and the Mind Warp的首张专辑，将现代前卫摇滚的厚重感与经典prog的织体相融合。主创Selvini是多乐器演奏家，乐队以五人编制呈现。专辑前半部分由四首五至九分钟的曲目组成，氛围轻盈段落以原声与清音吉他搭配氛围键盘，营造孤寂而幽暗的空间感；后半部分由一首长达二十六分钟的同名曲占据，重型段落具有后In Absentia时期Porcupine Tree的质感，棱角分明且带有数学摇滚的急促感。明暗两种情绪交替贯穿全作，Wall时期Pink Floyd式吉他riff的引用增添了阴暗底色。乐评指出其人声与吉他线条与美国乐队The Tea Club高度相似，尽管可能纯属巧合。整体而言，这张专辑以沉稳的结构对比和现代重型纹理为特色，在意大利前卫摇滚版图中呈现出偏离传统RPI路线的国际化面貌。

items.body: Chicago dark synth / industrial artist TATV GRAL returns to Side-Line.com with the exclusive video premiereof the DSTR remix of ‘Treachery’, launching alongside the four-track Treachery remix EP. While the original single explores the collision of opposing archetypal forces through a contemporary industrial and dark electronic lens, the remix EP extends the work in another direction, bringing together four distinct interpretations of the song: the original single version produced by William Faith, alongside reinterpretations by DSTR (Daniel Myer of Haujobb), Tweaker (Chris Vrenna of NIN), and fellow Chicago industrial outfit [melter]. Together, they gradually revealed an unexpected narrative to TATV GRAL’s Allen Addington only after the project was complete. Discussing the DSTR remix, Addington says: “I asked Daniel to find something in the song I hadn’t expressed myself – a different vantage on it. He pitched my voice down until it felt like I was speaking through a mask and built the track around a sense of searching rather than arrival. It also felt fitting, given Haujobb’s own homage to Front 242’s ‘Headhunter’ video on ‘We Must Wait’ featuring Jean-Luc De Meyer. Daniel already works within that lineage of one generation nodding to the last. It was only once I had all the remixes back that I recognized a narrative running through them alongside my original. DSTR is the search. [melter]’s mix is the extreme of the moment itself. Tweaker’s is the reflective aftermath. I didn’t consciously plan that arc. It revealed itself only after all the remixes were finished, as though each artist had uncovered a different aspect of the same song. I’m hoping to make two more videos to complete that story.” That same sense of continuity informed the accompanying video, which relocates the song from the symbolic interior spaces of the original clip into Chicago’s historic industrial landscape. Rather than using the city simply as a backdrop, Addington approached it as part of the visual and cultural lineage that shaped the music itself. “I shot it in Bridgeport neighbourhood of Chicago, where I live – the same industrial corridors Front Line Assembly used for ‘Isolate’ and KMFDM for ‘Vogue.’ It’s WAX TRAX! territory. Those same streets have appeared recently in Batman films, which says something about how this city’s decay keeps getting recast as myth. I wanted to uncover the history still present in that landscape – the industrial current that’s been there all along. All the glitch work is hand-built too: no plugins, no AI. Four bars might mean 64 individually designed frames, one at a time. That’s a small homage to where this graphic language actually comes from – hands cutting and layering images long before anyone had a filter to do it for them.” Tatv Gral’s ‘Treachery’ DSTR remix and the ‘Treachery EP’ The “Treachery EP” runs four tracks: the original “Treachery”, the DSTR remix by Daniel Myer, a remix by Chicago act [melter], and a version by Tweaker, the project of Chris Vrenna. The DSTR remix carries the video premiering here. Tatv Gral self-released the original “Treachery” single in June 2026, produced by William Faith at 13 Studio in Chicago. Treachery EP by Tatv Gral About Tatv Gral Tatv Gral is the solo project of Allen Addington, a multimedia artist based in Chicago, Illinois, active since the mid-1990s. The project mixes dark synth and industrial electronics with themes drawn from archetypal psychology and a queer leather aesthetic. Addington issued the debut “The Chase” in May 2019, followed by “Chiron” in June 2019, “Soul Divine” in March 2020 and “Noncommittal Grey” in March 2023. In March 2025 Tatv Gral appeared as a guest at the release show for The Funeral March‘s final album “It All Falls Apart”, alongside [melter] and William Faith. The “Treachery” single arrived in June 2026, and the “Treachery EP” now gathers it with the DSTR, [melter] and Tweaker remixes, led by the Daniel Myer video premiering on Side-Line.
items._cn_summary: 芝加哥暗黑合成器与工业艺人TATV GRAL发行《Treachery》混音EP，收录原版及DSTR、Tweaker、melter三位remixer的重新诠释。原文由William Faith制作原曲，Daniel Myer将人声降至低沉如戴面具般的效果，围绕探索感构建音轨；Tweaker则呈现内省式反思，melter捕捉极端情绪时刻，艺术家在收齐混音后才察觉一条无意识贯穿的叙事弧线。MV在芝加哥Bridgeport工业区取景，与Front Line Assembly、KMFDM的工业历史脉络形成视觉对话。视觉故障效果全部手工逐帧制作，无插件或AI介入，致敬切割叠层图像的早期图形语言传统。整体呈现出对工业音乐谱系的自觉承续与跨代致敬。

items.body: Les Hérauts de l’Ombre, a dark-electronic collective based in Verviers, Belgium, released their debut “Compilation” on 21 June 2026 through Bandcamp. The self-released set runs nine tracks and gathers three solo projects – NIAC, Obtenebrate and Anomaly 2.0 – that move between synthwave, darkwave and industrial EBM. Compilation by Les Hérauts de l’Ombre Inside Les Hérauts de l’Ombre’s ‘Compilation’ “Compilation” gives each project three tracks. NIAC, the darksynth project of Steve Fabry, contributes “Ashes where angels fell”, “Last sin before dawn” and “No prayers for the Innoncent”. Obtenebrate adds the darkwave tracks “Raging”, “The Decline” and “The Nameless God”. Anomaly 2.0, the EBM project of Togk, closes each rotation with “Blood Economy”, “Memories” and “Surveillance symphony”. The collective describe themselves as a French-Belgian group built to unite three complementary identities under one banner, and present the three acts as a continuous live set. “Compilation” is their first joint release and serves as an introduction to all three projects on a single record. About Les Hérauts de l’Ombre Les Hérauts de l’Ombre is a dark-electronic collective centred in Verviers, Belgium, formed around three solo projects. NIAC is the project of Steve Fabry, who records cinematic darksynth influenced by John Carpenter and released the album “Neo-Pandemonium” in 2020; he also records under the name The Nightstalker. Anomaly 2.0 is the electronic project of Togk, previously part of the acts Under All and Zorglüb. Obtenebrate rounds out the collective on the darkwave side. Each project maintains its own catalogue on Bandcamp, and “Compilation” marks the first time the three appear together under the Les Hérauts de l’Ombre name. The release sets a starting point for the collective’s shared output and live performances.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑汇集了比利时Verviers暗电子集体旗下三个独立项目的作品，各分配三首曲目。NIAC贡献受John Carpenter影响的电影感暗合成器段落，Obtenebrate提供暗潮方向的曲目，Anomaly 2.0以EBM工业节拍收尾每轮播放。集体将三者定位为可连续演出的互补身份，统一在'暗影使者'名义下首次联合发行。作为自发行作品，专辑充当三个项目的入门介绍，展示其在暗电子光谱内不同子类型间的游走能力，但本质上是已有各自Bandcamp目录曲目的汇编，缺乏专辑整体的统一叙事或深层结构创新。

items._cn_summary: 这是一张由DJ S.Y.D混音的电子合辑，以Ambient、Drone、Noise、Experimental为核心风格，精选33首横跨实验电子、当代古典与具象音乐的作品。曲目选择从关迺忠的古琴、谢斯可斯的音响建筑，到皮埃尔·亨利的具体音乐，再到池田亮司的数字化声音处理，跨度极大。混音将不同时代、不同地域的声音碎片串联成一条连续的意识流，淡化原始曲目的语境，强调声响本身的物质性与空间感。选曲涵盖Cindytalk、Pita、Kevin Drumm、Colin Stetson等地下实验圈重要人物，体现了对前卫聆听传统的熟稔。作为一份混音作品，其价值在于编排思路而非原创内容，适合作为背景聆听或声音研究素材。独立厂牌发行，法国制作，地域属性并不突出。整体而言，选曲品味扎实，但缺乏文字评论支撑，无法深入评估其艺术主张。

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由独立厂牌Recital发行，为庆祝厂牌五周年而作，收录了二十位艺术家的作品，横跨实验电子、当代古典与声音艺术等多个领域。曲目从Roger Eno的钢琴三重奏到Ian William Craig改编自John Keats诗作的人声作品，从Giovanni Fontana的声响拼贴到Loren Connors的吉他即兴，展现出策展人Sean McCann对地下实验音乐场景的广泛涉猎。Adriano Spatola的具象诗朗诵、Charlie Morrow为Dick Higgins创作的铜管作品等，呈现出强烈的先锋艺术倾向。整张合辑作为厂牌五年成果的回顾，强调跨媒介、跨流派的探索精神，但曲目之间风格跳跃较大，缺乏统一的美学线索，更适合作为了解当代实验音乐生态的索引式聆听材料。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴手与两位挪威乐手组成三重奏，对斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲进行非传统演绎。乐评将其比作室内乐，三位乐手沉浸在亲密的音乐对话中，而非为舞蹈伴奏，更像是探索音乐中隐藏的意义与神秘感。编曲以传统旋律为出发点，加入自由即兴与音色实验，竖笛、小提琴与鼓的组合营造出时而碎片化、时而统一的声响纹理。乐评特别提及开篇曲目与挪威民间传说中瀑布精灵的关联，暗示传统舞曲表层欢快之下可能存在的暗流。独立小厂牌发行，整体定位介于世界音乐、学院派即兴与实验民谣之间。

items._cn_summary: 西班牙吉他手 Dani Jané 的第三张专辑融合弗拉门戈、加泰罗尼亚民谣、古典、爵士与诗歌元素，呈现多元文化语境下的器乐对话。专辑以吉他为核心，与长笛、打击乐及效果器构建层次丰富的声景，多首曲目如《El vol de la Vida》将华特·惠特曼的诗作以西班牙语译本嵌入古典组曲结构，尾声融入 bulerías 演唱。家族情感贯穿其中，《Les penes de l'amar》取材于其祖父1938年创作的歌词，rumba 节奏承载家族记忆；《Milonga C.F. 2.0》以家乡 Can Finestres 命名，回溯童年学琴经历。录音汇集巴塞罗那多位乐手，flamenco 歌手、低音提琴与鼓手为核心四重奏增添厚重底色。最终曲目《Lydda》由加泰隆尼亚吉他大师 Toti Soler 创作，吉他与长笛在卡纳提克风格的人声打击乐点缀下交替推进。整体展现了新一代加泰罗尼亚学院派艺术家在弗拉门戈之外拓展语言边界的尝试。

items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?
items.label: Ponderosa Music
items._cn_summary: 专辑纪念意大利南部撒伦托地区的pizzica音乐传统走过半个世纪，由乐队创始人之子Mauro Durante带领新一代乐手重新演绎早期作品。老一辈成员Rina与Daniele Durante的创作被年轻一代的演奏赋予新色彩和编曲，保留原声乐器为主的同时加入少量电子元素如合成贝斯。乐评特别提到与钢琴家Ludovico Einaudi合作的Taranta项目混音版本被收录其中。多位早期歌手回归献声，专辑既是致敬也是跨越代际的对话，展示了这种源自意大利南部的地方音乐如何从区域传统走向全球舞台，在保持文化根源的同时不断演化。

items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴演奏家Teija Niku的第四张专辑融合了北欧与巴尔干民间音乐传统，历经疫情、生育与丧母等人生转折后完成。专辑以北欧感性为底色，融入保加利亚民间舞曲节奏、马其顿情歌元素，辅以明快的波兰舞曲节奏。Niku展现出敏锐的旋律感，如《Elokuu》以轻快旋律捕捉八月夏末光影中夹杂的冬日预感。压轴曲《Poloneesi Äidille》为她母亲七十岁生日所作，三年后母亲离世，柔美挽歌在她开口吟唱的瞬间升华为超越性的情感表达。专辑在民谣与世界音乐范畴内完成了真诚的跨文化探索，但在实验性或前卫元素上较为有限。

items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items.body: Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gon�alves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell�s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, �Birthday Song� comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, �I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.� The record closes with �Overture,� anchored by Gon�alves� dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe�s Japanese exhortation, �Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.� Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father�s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. �Snow� begins with Makabe�s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while �Text� swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe�s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe �Morisan� hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Remembering the future is really just looking at the past, isn't it? It is a matter of interpretation, much like the content of this conceptual work, which tells the story of an extraterrestrial named Bluebird. Bluebird communicates with a blind child, sharing knowledge about human evolution, the origins of Earth, and humanity's destiny; the child's unique ability suggests that understanding and feeling may be more important than what is seen, which is often confusing and deceptive. Things are not what they seem, and despite a cover that promises a wild, crazy world..."Remember the Future - Part I" truly seems to begin during the latter part of the title track, featuring a guitar solo accompanied by organ that evokes freer, wilder times. It also brings to mind the astral journeys of the Welsh band Man, who had also dabbled in the Krautrock sound in the past. "Confusion," its final section, truly dives deep into the ocean and breathes something other than oxygen; Roye Albrighton's guitar plays, yet also cuts and stings, followed by Allan "Taff" Freeman's distinctly progressive keyboards.The same applies to the second part, (Remember the Future - Part II) and upon reaching "Tomorrow Never Comes", the third section within it, it is Roye's guitar notes that draw us into labyrinths that shift from the spiral of a snail shell to the labyrinth of the inner ear.Some notes were reminiscent of David Gilmour, before ending with a strong Doobie Brothers vibe in Let It Grow. The iconic cover was created by Helmut Wenske, also known by the alias Chris Hyde, a German illustrator and musician who had also designed A Tab in the Ocean in 1972.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / space rock / progressive rock / Krautrock-influenced
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1973年发行的概念专辑，讲述了一个名为Bluebird的外星生命与失明儿童交流的故事，主题涉及人类进化、地球起源与命运。乐评指出音乐从标题曲后半段才真正开始，吉他独奏与风琴交织，营造出自由狂野的氛围，乐手Roye Albrighton的吉他时而流畅时而尖锐，配以Allan Freeman的键盘形成典型的70年代前摇编制。第二部分延续了迷宫般的器乐探索，某些段落让人联想到David Gilmour的吉他风格，结尾的Let It Grow则带有Doobie Brothers的味道。封面由德国插画家Helmut Wenske设计，与1972年专辑A Tab in the Ocean出自同一人。整体而言，这是一张带有迷幻与太空摇滚色彩的概念专辑，在器乐编排上展现了70年代英国前摇的特征，但对于追求更极端实验、自由即兴或电子融合的听众而言，其创新边界相对有限。
